Visit note | 2026-06-07 03:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Gautam Sen, 41, male. Mr. Sen attends for review regarding his ongoing respiratory symptoms, reporting a tight chest when exposed to dust or cold air, coughing at night, and noticeable wheezing. He works as a hotel receptionist and mentions his symptoms have been worse since construction dust started near his home in Farmgate. He has no significant comorbidities and denies fever or chest pain. On examination: SpO2 92%, BP 132/78 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 52 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued for controller and relief therapy. He was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep his bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.
